category_title: Students with autism displaying sensory-seeking vocalizations
minimal_context: The student is gathered on the floor with the whole class for a circle time activity.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Alright everyone, please sit on the floor so we can begin our circle time activity.

STUDENT: (Sits on the floor but begins making humming and mouth noises.)

TUTOR: Rick, please stop making those noises.

STUDENT: (Looks up, smiles, and continues making the mouth noises.)

TUTOR: You need to stop; otherwise you will have to leave.

STUDENT: (Becomes clearly agitated, continues the noises, and pulls away) Noooo!

options.A: Provide support using the 'quiet' picture card to help him stop the noises instead of taking him outside.
options.B: Call attention to a new activity by asking the class to put their hands up, slap the floor twice, and say 'Circle time!'
options.C: Ask him to think of a question about the circle time activity that he would like to discuss.
options.D: Reinforce the desired behavior with a high five or a verbal compliment when he stops making the noises.
